answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, whether sourcing walnut, pricing quartz, or shipping willow. Creating extra names grants no free capacity: an attacker running 10,000 eligible identities must immobilize $1 million for the full period. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes a swarm costly by tying every active identity to locked capital.
